messages:
maria: heads-up: deploy-bot flagged a degraded path during the canary for v2.4.1. thinking we should prep a short maintenance/rollback comms and a statuspage snippet in case we need a brief change window.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout halted at 10:32 UTC — fallback to regional pool triggered for 3% traffic. Error: kv-cache-miss spike. Logs: `error: kvcache::miss_rate=0.23`

kevin: thanks — can we confirm scope? is it only Hosted API? Dedicated/private unaffected?

sam: Dedicated unaffected, Private customers on-prem unaffected. Hosted endpoints seeing elevated latencies for some long-seq gen workloads. No data loss.

lina: ok, customer-facing: we should avoid alarming language. short status: "Investigating elevated latency for Hosted API; some requests routed to fallback capacity. No data loss."", longer note for support emails with rollback options + estimated window.

maria: draft statuspage snippet (short): "Investigating increased latency on Hosted API; automatic fallback routing in effect. We’re monitoring; no customer data impacted. ETA next update: 30 minutes."

kevin: +1. add mention: "Customers with strict latency SLOs can temporarily pin to dedicated model variants via the console — contact support for help."

sam: rollback decision: if fallback continues past 45m and error rates >1% for requests with seq >1024, we abort v2.4.1 and pin back to v2.4.0 for Hosted. Ops runbook ready.

maria: include contact line and escalation: support@redwood.ai and Priority phone for enterprise customers. Also add planned change window only if we need to take a short outage for rollback (max 15m).

lina: email template draft (short):
```
Subject: Maintenance notice — brief: possible latency impact on Hosted API
Hi — We’re investigating increased latency affecting some Hosted API requests. Automatic fallback routing is active; no customer data impacted. If we need to perform a short rollback with a brief change window (<=15 minutes) we will notify again and post updates to status.redwood.ai. For assistance, reply here or contact support@redwood.ai.
```

maria: statusbot — please schedule an initial statuspage post with the short snippet and set auto-update reminder in 30m.

statusbot: Scheduled: Initial update posted to status.redwood.ai/incidents/1925 at 10:35 UTC. Auto-reminder set for 30 minutes.

kevin: also ping Legal for any enterprise contracts needing notice? I think not for <15m.

sam: ops: we’ll watch for kv-cache-miss >0.2 sustained for 10m => action: pin back + shard-rebalance. I’ll own the rollback if needed, lina can own customer comms while maria coordinates with SRE.

lina: noted. I’ll prep a canned sequence for status updates: 1) investigating, 2) mitigation in progress, 3) rollback executed (if), 4) resolved + postmortem ETA.

maria: perfect. final ask — Lina, paste the exact statuspage copy you want me to post if we escalate to a change window.

lina: paste for change-window (15m):
```
We will perform a short maintenance window (up to 15 minutes) to roll back Hosted API to v2.4.0 to restore latency SLOs. During this window some API requests may fail with 5xx. We expect normal operation to resume immediately after rollback. Updates will be posted here and via email to subscribers.
```

maria: saved. I’ll post the initial short update and keep this thread for live edits. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary resume blocked until kv-cache patch deployed. Manual rollback command available: `infra rollback --service=hosted-api --to-version=2.4.0 --force`

sam: copying rollback command into ops-run. standing by.

lina: prepping customer email list + enterprise phone list now.

maria: closing loop — initial post live. will update at 30m or earlier if we rollback.
